subject.title: Embedded runner: freshly streamed thinking signatures intermittently invalid on replay (Anthropic); recovery wrapper never fires because error text is genericized

question: Which Anthropic signed-thinking prevention path should become canonical for this issue: the scoped current-turn replay fix in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99383, the broader sanitizer in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100149, or a recovery-only/defer-prevention path?
rationale: Current main has partial recovery fixes, but the remaining prevention choice changes provider replay semantics for Claude thinking blocks and overlaps multiple active PRs, so automation should not choose the product/compatibility direction alone.

options.title: Land scoped replay policy
options.body: Review and, if still clean, land the scoped SDK plus managed-transport current-turn replay fix in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99383 and close the broader cluster after release proof.

options.title: Adopt broader sanitizer
options.body: Pause the scoped PRs and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100149 or a replacement if maintainers want a central sanitizer to strip non-latest signatures across more surfaces.

options.title: Recovery only for now
options.body: Keep prevention open and rely on merged recovery paths temporarily, accepting that thinking-enabled sessions can still pay a one-shot rejection or depend on runtime retry behavior.

recommendation.title: Land scoped replay policy
recommendation.body: Review and, if still clean, land the scoped SDK plus managed-transport current-turn replay fix in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99383 and close the broader cluster after release proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice centers on Claude thinking replay preservation policy, which Qinyao He introduced in the current helper history.
